terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Run the departures board here, and print what you make to see it.

tasks.title: Is the boat full?
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 1` in `Departures.java`, make a `boolean` called `full`: `true` when `passengers` is equal to `seats` or more, `false` otherwise.

Check runs your Task 1 lines with crossings of its own, including one where the passengers exactly fill the seats, and reads `full`.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson about comparisons.
Pick the comparison that is true for equal numbers too.
Make `full` with it, print it and run the program.
Change `passengers` at the top to 48 for a moment and run again, then change it back.
hints: A comparison between two numbers is itself a value: `true` or `false`. It can go straight into a `boolean`.
`>` is false when the two are equal. The comparison for "equal or more" is written with two characters.
The line has the shape `boolean full = passengers >= ...;`.

tasks.title: Can the boat sail?
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 2`, Ossian sails when the wind is below 30 knots and there is no fog. Make a `boolean` called `canSail`: `true` when both are so, `false` otherwise. The wind is in `windKnots` and the fog in `fog`, a `boolean`.

Check runs your Task 2 lines with weather of its own, including a wind of exactly 30 knots, and reads `canSail`.
nextSteps: Write the two conditions on their own first: the wind one and the fog one.
Read the part of the lesson about joining conditions.
Join them so both must be true.
Print `canSail` and try a few winds at the top of the file.
hints: "Below 30" leaves out 30 itself. "No fog" is the opposite of `fog`.
`&&` is true only when both sides are true. `!` in front of a `boolean` turns true into false and false into true.
The line has the shape `boolean canSail = windKnots < 30 && ...;`.

tasks.title: Set the board
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 3`, make a `String` called `status` for the departures board: `Cancelled` when the boat cannot sail, otherwise `Full` when the boat is full, otherwise `Boarding`. `canSail` and `full` from Tasks 1 and 2 already say both.

Check runs your Tasks 1, 2 and 3 with crossings of its own, including a full boat in fog, and reads `status`.
nextSteps: Make sure Tasks 1 and 2 pass first: this one builds on them.
Make `status` first, then decide its value with `if`, `else if` and `else`.
Think about which check has to come first when the boat is both full and cannot sail.
Print `status` and try a few values at the top of the file.
hints: Java takes the first branch whose condition is true and skips all the others.
A cancelled crossing is cancelled however full the boat is, so that check goes first. Every branch gives `status` a value, or the compiler says it might not have been initialized.
The shape is `String status;` then `if (!canSail) { status = ...; } else if (full) { status = ...; } else { status = ...; }`.

tasks.title: Charge the right fare
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 4`, make an `int` called `farePence` for one passenger of this `age`: children under 5 travel free, children under 16 pay half of `singleFarePence`, everyone else pays `singleFarePence`.

Check runs your Task 4 lines with ages and fares of its own, including ages 5 and 16 exactly, and reads `farePence`.
nextSteps: List the three groups of passengers and what each pays.
Decide the order of the checks: a child of 3 is also under 16.
Print it and try ages 3, 5, 15 and 16 at the top of the file.
hints: Java takes the first branch whose condition is true. Which check must come first so a child of 3 travels free?
Under 5 is `age < 5`, under 16 is `age < 16`. Half the fare is the fare divided by 2.
The shape is `int farePence;` then `if (age < 5) { ... } else if (age < 16) { ... } else { ... }`, each branch giving `farePence` its value.
